extracted.intended_audience: students, educators, and mathematicians interested in problem-solving, heuristics, and forming mathematical conjectures
extracted.subtask_description: Heuristics and patterns for guessing, forming, and assessing mathematical conjectures and plausible inferences; guidance aimed at learners and practitioners who want to improve informal discovery and justification techniques in mathematics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value of guessing alongside proving
rubrics_metrics.description: Certainly, let us learn proving, but also let us learn guessing. A good guess is as important as a good proof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Polya exhorts students to develop the skill of making plausible guesses (conjectures) in addition to learning formal proof techniques; cultivate conjecturing as part of mathematical practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Induction (as a method of guessing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Induction, not mathematical induction, but as a way of guessing new results: observing a few instances can prompt formulation of conjectures (example: observations 4=2+2, 6=3+3, 8=3+5, 10=3+7 may prompt Goldbach's conjecture).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use concrete examples and patterns in small cases to form conjectures; Polya illustrates with example sequences and problems (e.g., sequence 11,31,41,61,71,101,131...). Induction here is informal pattern-based inference rather than formal proof by induction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of generalization, specialization, and analogy
rubrics_metrics.description: Generalization, specialization and analogy are presented as possible strategies for plausible reasoning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply these techniques to move between specific cases and broader statements (generalize), test conjectures by focusing on particular cases (specialize), and transfer insights between similar contexts (analogy) when searching for or justifying conjectures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relate plausible inference patterns to probability
rubrics_metrics.description: Volume II attempts to formulate certain patterns of plausible reasoning and investigates their relation with the calculus of probability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess how patterns of inference affect the credibility of conjectures probabilistically; use probability calculus as a framework to compare and weigh plausible conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pattern 1: A implies B; B true ⇒ A more credible
rubrics_metrics.description: Premise 1: A implies B. Premise 2: B is true. Plausible conclusion: A is more credible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a hypothesis would imply an observed consequence, the observation increases the credibility of the hypothesis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pattern 2: A implies B and B_{n+1} very different from former consequences ⇒ A much more credible
rubrics_metrics.description: Premise 1: A implies B_{n+1}. Premise 2: B_{n+1} is very different from the formerly verified consequences B_1, B_2, ..., B_n of A. Premise 3: B_{n+1} true. Plausible conclusion: A much more credible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An unexpected, novel consequence of a hypothesis that is verified greatly increases the hypothesis's credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pattern 3: A implies B_{n+1} similar to former consequences ⇒ A just a little more credible
rubrics_metrics.description: Premise 1: A implies B_{n+1}. Premise 2: B_{n+1} is very similar to the formerly verified consequences B_1, B_2, ..., B_n of A. Premise 3: B_{n+1} true. Plausible conclusion: A just a little more credible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A new consequence that is similar to previously verified ones provides only a small additional credibility boost to the hypothesis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pattern 4: A implies B; B improbable but true ⇒ A very much more credible
rubrics_metrics.description: Premise 1: A implies B. Premise 2: B is very improbable in itself. Premise 3: B is true. Plausible conclusion: A very much more credible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a hypothesis predicts an event that would be very unlikely otherwise, and that event occurs, the hypothesis gains strong credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pattern 5: A implies B; B quite probable and true ⇒ A just a little more credible
rubrics_metrics.description: Premise 1: A implies B. Premise 2: B is quite probable in itself. Premise 3: B is true. Plausible conclusion: A is just a little more credible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observing a consequence that was already likely does not substantially increase credibility of the hypothesis that predicts it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pattern 6: A analogous to B; B true ⇒ A more credible
rubrics_metrics.description: Premise: A analogous to B. Premise: B is true. Plausible conclusion: A is more credible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By analogy to a known true case, a similar conjecture becomes more credible; analogical evidence increases plausibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pattern 7: A analogous to B; B more credible ⇒ A somewhat more credible
rubrics_metrics.description: Premise: A analogous to B. Premise: B is more credible. Plausible conclusion: A is somewhat more credible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a well-supported case exists, by analogy a related hypothesis gains some, but limited, credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pattern 8: A is implied by B; B false ⇒ A less credible
rubrics_metrics.description: Premise: A is implied by B. Premise: B is false. Plausible conclusion: A is less credible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a stronger hypothesis that would imply the statement is refuted, that undermines the credibility of the implied statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pattern 9: A incompatible with B; B false ⇒ A more credible
rubrics_metrics.description: Premise: A is incompatible with B. Premise: B is false. Plausible conclusion: A is more credible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refutation of a hypothesis incompatible with A increases the relative credibility of A.
